title: One van, then a nation
note: Abdul Sattar Edhi grew one donated van into the world's largest volunteer ambulance service, asking no one's faith.

research.quotes: heroes.html#abdul-sattar-edhi: 'in 1951 bought a tiny dispensary.' 'A donation bought a battered old van, and Edhi himself drove it to accidents, floods, and riots. From that van grew what Guinness World Records recognized as the world's largest volunteer ambulance network.' 'homes for orphans, the disabled, the mentally ill, and abandoned women; kitchens; morgues.' 'because the ambulance is more Muslim than you.'
research.retell: A poor cloth seller named Edhi turned one donated van into the world's largest volunteer ambulance fleet that helps anyone, whatever their faith.

lines.text: One old van became a giant rescue fleet
lines.sub: the largest volunteer fleet on earth
Abdul Sattar Edhi, a poor cloth seller

lines.text: He opens a tiny free clinic
A donation buys one battered van
lines.sub: Edhi drives it himself to every disaster

lines.text: From that van grows a whole fleet
Outside each centre he puts a cradle
lines.sub: so no unwanted baby is ever killed

lines.text: Critics asked why he carried non Muslims
lines.sub: the ambulance is more Muslim than you

lines.text: His ambulances still ask no one's faith
He owned two sets of clothes
